slides.title: Human-Robot Interaction: Introduction
slides.text:
Human-Robot Interaction: Introduction

•   HRI is the interdisciplinary study of interaction dynamics between humans and robotic systems.
•   Interaction channels are categorized as:                                                                     Intel
    –  verbal (spoken language),                                                                 RealSense
                                                                                                              D435i(for
    –  non-verbal (facial expression, gesture, gaze, proximity),                                                                                                          nonverbal)
    –  and physical (touch, manipulation).
•   HRI systems increasingly rely on learned, data-driven perception
   and dialogue components.
•   AI enhances perception, reasoning, and conversational capabilities.
                                                                                                                                     [1]•   Social intelligence enables robots to understand human intentions.
•   Emotion-aware communication improves user engagement and
    collaboration.
•   Trust calibration in HRI depends on socially appropriate and contextually
   grounded robot responses.
•   Natural interaction improves user acceptance and trust.
•   HRI is widely used in healthcare, education, industries, and service robotics.

                                                                                                            3

visualInspection.notes: Full text and annotated humanoid photograph inspected. Definition/interdisciplinary HRI; verbal speech, nonverbal expression/gesture/gaze/proximity, physical touch/manipulation. Torso camera circled and labeled Intel RealSense D435i for nonverbal; speaker icon. Trust calibration requires contextual/social appropriateness, not maximum trust. General benefit claims are goals, not measured causal results. Footer3.

slides.title: Multi-Modal Artificial Intelligence in Robotics
slides.text:
Multi-Modal Artificial Intelligence in Robotics
•  A modality represents a distinct source of information, such as vision, speech, or text.
•   Multi-modal AI combines information from multiple sensory inputs.
•   Vision provides environmental and behavioral understanding.
•   Speech enables natural human-machine communication.
•   Data fusion improves decision accuracy and contextual awareness.
•   Multi-modal systems are more robust than single-modality systems.
•   Emotion-aware robots integrate visual perception with conversational intelligence.
•   The central technical challenge in multi-modal AI is the cross-modal fusion problem.
•   Fusion strategies include early fusion, late fusion, and hybrid
    intermediate-representation fusion.
•   This system fuses modalities by converting visual output into a natural
    language description.
•   Language-mediated fusion allows a language model to reason jointly
    over multiple signal types.
•   This fusion pattern generalizes to any structured signal expressible in textual form.

                                                                                                            4

visualInspection.notes: Actual multimodal bullets and speech-plus-camera graphic inspected. Modality defined; early/late/hybrid-intermediate fusion named but not formalized. This system converts visual output to natural-language description; language-mediated fusion generalizes to textual structured signals. Blanket robustness/accuracy statements require conditions; text conversion can discard information and poor/late inputs can harm decisions. Footer4.

slides.title: Face Detection Pipeline
slides.text:
Face Detection Pipeline

•   The cropped facial image is resized to match the neural network input resolution.
                                                                                                      Input Image
•    Pixel intensity normalization improves consistency across different lighting conditions.
•   Convolutional layers extract local texture and facial appearance features.
                                                                                               Face Detector•   Deeper network layers learn abstract emotional representations.
•   Feature vectors are transformed into emotion probabilities through a Softmax classifier.
•   The emotion with the highest confidence score is selected as the final prediction.           Bounding Box
•   Confidence thresholds reduce uncertain or ambiguous classifications.
•    Final emotion labels are published through ROS2 middleware for downstream processing.     Face Crop
•   The complete inference pipeline operates continuously to support real-time interaction.





                                                          Face detected and
                                                        cropped



                                                                                                            9

visualInspection.notes: Actual heading Face Detection Pipeline but bullets include expression-network resizing, normalization, convolution features, abstract features, Softmax, argmax and confidence filtering. Right diagram itself ends at face crop. Lower live-view screenshot shows face box and text overlays; tiny numerical labels need enlarged revisit before use. Distinguish detection from emotion classification; no specific input resolution or threshold value supplied. Footer9. Enlarged original PDF screenshot revisited: green ROI, Neutral label and speech/robot transcript overlays; top and bottom FPS fields differ, so no stable FPS benchmark inferred. slides.text:
DeepFace-Based Facial Emotion Recognition                                                                                               Face crop
•   DeepFace performs facial attribute and emotion analysis.
•   Cropped facial images are processed using pretrained deep neural networks.                                                                                        DeepFace
•    Facial features are extracted automatically during inference.
•   The model classifies expressions into predefined emotion categories.
                                                                                              Feature Extraction
•   Predicted emotions include Happy, Sad, Angry, Neutral, Fear, Surprise, and Disgust.
•   Confidence scores indicate prediction reliability.
•   Low-confidence predictions can be filtered to improve system robustness.            Emotion Classification
•   Emotion labels provide contextual information for conversational response generation.
•   Real-time inference enables emotionally adaptive human-robot interaction.



                                                        Emotion Recognized





                                                                                                           10

Pretrained inference is not online training. Screenshot has log, green box and neutral label; precise score requires crop revisit. Confidence as reliability is not a calibrated correctness probability or proof of inner emotion. Footer10. Enlarged original PDF screenshot revisited: highlighted Emotion: Neutral (94%); upper live-view FPS30.5; console shows alternating Neutral/Angry detections, Speech detected and Processing. These are saved displayed predictions, not validation labels or a measured94% accuracy.

slides.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence
slides.text:
Conversational Artificial Intelligence
•   Conversational AI enables robots to communicate naturally using
    spoken language and contextual understanding.
•   Modern conversational systems integrate speech processing, language
    understanding, reasoning, and response generation into a unified framework.
•   Natural language interaction significantly improves user                   Conversational AI Pipeline
    engagement and accessibility in robotic applications.                                  Response                                                                                                      Speaker                                                                   Open AI API                                                                Microphone
•   Large Language Models (LLMs) enable context-aware                                    Genration
    conversations by understanding user intent and maintaining
    dialogue continuity.
•   Real-time conversational systems prioritize low response
    latency to achieve natural human-like communication.
•   Context management enables robots to generate coherent responses
    throughout multi-turn conversations.
•   Emotion-aware dialogue adapts the tone and style of responses based on
    contextual information from perception systems.
•   Conversational AI is widely adopted in healthcare, customer service, education, and assistive robotics.

                                                                                                           11

visualInspection.notes: Actual text and microphone→API→response→speaker diagram inspected. Spoken interaction combines speech understanding, reasoning, generation; multiturm context; low latency; emotion adapts tone/style. Contextual visual cue does not override explicit user request; usage domains are examples not clinical effectiveness proof. Footer11.

slides.title: OpenAI Realtime API Architecture                           WebSocket Session
slides.text:
OpenAI Realtime API Architecture                           WebSocket Session
                                                                                      Audio Stream Input•   OpenAI Realtime API enables continuous voice-to-voice interaction
    through persistent bidirectional communication.                                                                                   Speech Understanding
•   Audio streams are transmitted using WebSocket-based
                                                                                             Conversation Context    communication instead of conventional request-response protocols.
•   Incoming speech is processed continuously without requiring                        Language Reasoning
    complete audio recordings.
                                                                                     Speech Synthesis•   Speech understanding, language reasoning, and
    speech generation are performed within a unified AI pipeline.                                                                                         Streaming Audio Output
•   Incremental audio streaming significantly reduces conversational response latency.
•   Event-driven communication allows the server to process and respond dynamically to user interactions.
•   Continuous streaming enables smooth interruption handling during active
    conversations.
•    Persistent sessions maintain conversational context throughout the
     interaction.
•   The architecture supports scalable, low-latency conversational intelligence
     for robotic applications.

                                                                                                           12

visualInspection.notes: Actual Realtime architecture bullets and vertical diagram inspected: WebSocket session→audio input→speech understanding→conversation context→reasoning→synthesis→streaming output. Persistent bidirectional event-driven stream; incremental audio not whole recording. Session not unlimited history. Interruption handling depends on client/configuration; WebSocket is chosen transport, not only possible API transport. This is conceptual, not mandatory explicit STT→text→TTS internal implementation. Footer12.

slides.text:
Session Created

                                                                                      Audio Buffer AppendEvent-Driven Voice Communication
•   Event-driven communication processes interactions as a sequence              Voice Activity Detection
    of independent events instead of isolated requests.                                                                                     Speech Transcription
•   User speech is continuously streamed from the microphone to
                                                                                              Conversation Context
    the conversational AI service.
•   Voice Activity Detection (VAD) automatically determines                           Language Model
    the beginning and end of speech segments.                                      Speech Synthesis
•   Speech events trigger language understanding and response generation
                                                                                             Audio
    without manual intervention.
•   Incremental transcripts are generated as speech is processed in real time.        Session Continues
•   Response audio is streamed progressively instead of waiting for complete synthesis.
•   Simultaneous audio transmission and reception enable full-duplex
    conversational interaction.
•   Automatic interruption handling prioritizes new user speech over
    ongoing system responses.
•   Event-driven architectures improve responsiveness and scalability in
    real-time robotic communication systems.

                                                                                                           13

visualInspection.notes: Actual event-driven prose and right sequence inspected: session created→audio buffer append→VAD→speech transcription→conversation context→language model→speech synthesis→audio→session continues. VAD locates speech boundaries, not intent. Full duplex sends/receives concurrently. Independent events does not mean unordered/statistically independent state. Transcript generation/configuration and interruption are implementation-dependent; no exact API event names or source code printed. Footer13.

slides.title: Audio Streaming and Response Generation
slides.text:
Audio Streaming and Response Generation

•   Microphone audio is continuously captured and converted into digital
    audio samples.
•   Audio frames are buffered and transmitted sequentially through
    persistent WebSocket connections.
•   Streaming protocols minimize communication
    overhead while maintaining continuous interaction.
•   The conversational AI processes incoming audio                                                   Speech streaming
    and generates contextual responses in real time.
•   Synthesized speech is streamed incrementally for immediate
    playback through the speaker.
•   Audio buffering compensates for network latency and ensures
    uninterrupted speech output.
•   User interruptions immediately terminate ongoing playback and initiate
   new response generation.
•   Low-latency streaming significantly improves the naturalness of
    human-robot conversations.

                                                                                                           14

visualInspection.notes: Actual streaming bullets and screenshot inspected: microphone digital samples, sequential buffers, persistent connection, incremental playback. Screenshot shows Neutral(88%) and speech/robot transcript overlays, topFPS28.9, bottomFPSdifferent; not timing benchmark. Buffering absorbs bounded jitter but cannot guarantee uninterrupted output for arbitrary network outage. Interruption cannot literally be zero-time or automatically flush every client queue without handling. Footer14.

slides.title: Visualization and System Monitoring
slides.text:
Visualization and System Monitoring





                                                                  [1]

•    Visualization tools provide real-time observation of system behavior during execution.
•   Annotated camera frames display detected faces, bounding boxes, and emotion predictions.
•   Emotion labels and confidence values are continuously updated during interaction.
•   ROS2 topic monitoring verifies successful communication between distributed nodes.
•   Console logs assist in identifying runtime errors and communication failures.
•   Session recording enables post-experimental analysis and system validation.
•   Monitoring tools simplify debugging, performance evaluation, and software
    maintenance.
•    Visualization improves the interpretability of AI-based robotic decision-making.
•   Comprehensive monitoring enhances reliability during real-world deployment.

                                                                                                           15

visualInspection.notes: Actual torso-screen→desktop screenshot and monitoring bullets inspected. Overlays expose boxes,labels,confidence; topic monitoring tests communication; logs expose failures; recordings support retrospective analysis. Visualization and node graph not proof of prediction correctness, freshness or ground-truth accuracy. Footer15.

slides.title: Emotion-Aware Prompt Engineering                                                                                     Emotion Label
slides.text:
Emotion-Aware Prompt Engineering                                                                                     Emotion Label
•   Prompt engineering defines how contextual information is
    presented to the language model.
•   Emotion predictions are transformed into structured                               Prompt Context
    natural language instructions.
•   The detected emotion is appended as supplementary conversational context.
•    Static prompts define the robot's personality, behavior,                              LLM
    and conversational objectives.
•   Dynamic prompts continuously update the user's current emotional
                                                                                     Context-Aware Response     state during interaction.
•   The language model prioritizes spoken user intent while considering emotional context.
•   Context management prevents redundant emotion updates from
    increasing conversation history.
•   Structured prompts improve response consistency and emotional
    appropriateness.
•   Prompt engineering enables adaptive dialogue without modifying the
    underlying language model.

                                                                                                           17

visualInspection.notes: Actual prompt bullets and four-box emotion label→prompt context→LLM→response inspected. Static personality/behavior/objectives versus dynamic estimated emotion. Spoken intent prioritized; deduplicate emotion updates to avoid history growth; prompting does not update model weights. No exact API calls/dedup algorithm/threshold printed; any trace must label supplied policy. Footer17.

slides.title: End-to-End System Data Flow
slides.text:
End-to-End System Data Flow





  •   The system simultaneously processes facial expressions and spoken input to
     enable multimodal human–robot interaction.
  •   Emotion recognition results are integrated with speech through ROS2 and
     OpenAI Realtime API to generate context-aware responses.
  •   The synthesized response is streamed to the robot speaker, enabling
     continuous real-time emotion-aware communication.


                                                                                                           18

visualInspection.notes: Actual full data-flow arrows traced: Human splits facial→RealSense→Face→DeepFaceEmotion→Emotion and speech→Microphone→Audio; both feed Context; then rightmost down to OpenAIRealtime; bottom flows RIGHT TO LEFT Speech→Language→Speech→Robot→Human. This is conceptual functional flow, not proof API internally requires separate transcripts. Bullets say parallel modalities and contextual integration before streamed response. Footer18.
